lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Viviane Rodrigues de Oliveira | Lesson 1 -- What You Actually Do
lesson.grammar_point: present simple for roles and responsibilities + question formation

listenings.text: I am the HR manager for a company with around six hundred people. My job is not really about paperwork. It is about culture. Every week I meet team leaders and I ask them the same three questions. What is working in your team? What is not working? And what do you need from me? I also run our engagement survey twice a year, and I read every single comment. Some of them are hard to read. Right now my main project is leadership development. We are building a programme for new managers, because most of our managers are excellent at their technical job and completely lost when they have to lead people. That is normal. Nobody teaches you that. So we teach it.

People always ask me what I listen for in an interview in English. Honestly, it is not perfect grammar. I interview candidates from twenty different countries and almost nobody speaks perfect English. What I listen for is whether you can tell me what you actually do. Not your job title. What you do. If I ask about your work and you give me three clear sentences with a real example, that is a strong candidate. If you give me a long list of responsibilities with no example, I stop listening after twenty seconds. And here is a small tip. When you do not understand my question, please just say so. Say: sorry, could you repeat that? Every good candidate does this. The ones who pretend to understand and answer the wrong question, those are the ones I remember for the wrong reason.

extra_audio.text: Hello, my name is Viviane. I work as an HR manager at a retail group. I am responsible for culture, performance and engagement. Right now I am building a leadership programme for new managers.
